model_input_audit.caveat: Input length T = 25U equals 25 x the number of keystrokes, so sequence length implicitly carries the original sentence length for every trial in both real and control conditions. Under the permutation this length matches the original, not the control, training target.

runtime_note: Laptop on battery (CPU throttled); 5U rerun took 45.4 min on the same code.

interpretation.classification: B. Real-label and no-signal performance are similar
interpretation.basis: The control memorized six mismatched signal/target pairs almost as well as real labels (train CER 0.043 vs 0.022). Held-out CER was 0.842 vs 0.841 for seed 123 and 1.047 vs 1.139 for seed 777 (control better); only seed 33 separated (1.356 vs 0.778). When real and control seeds land in the same blank regime (123: both ~97% blank; 777: both low-blank over-production) their CERs match; the single separating seed is the one where the control switched to the low-blank regime. The mean difference +0.162 is driven by that one seed.
caveats: Only two evaluation trials; no significance testing.
Does not prove absence of MEG character information; it shows this setup's held-out CER is not distinguishable from a mismatched-label model.
Input length T=25U implicitly encodes true sentence length in every condition.
